findings.title: No reading for rules that carry no keyword
findings.quote: library nevertheless uses the keywords for material claims where ordinary
findings.critique: The pattern defines strengths but gives no reading for a rule without one. In this slice the audit, Kubernetes, threat-modelling and webhook files contain no keyword, and the API, secrets and lifecycle files carry them only in sections added this month. For 'authenticate every protected route', nobody can say whether deviation needs an exception record, a noted reason, or nothing. The exception contract cannot operate on most of the security doctrine.
findings.recommendation: Add to section 1: until typed, an imperative in a principle or pattern is read as SHOULD within the file's stated scope; deviation needs a recorded reason when material and never an exception record. Then type the security owners first, starting with the candidates for MUST: server-side authorisation, encrypted transport, multi-factor authentication for production access, audit-record protection and leaked-secret response.

findings.title: Exception contract has one size, no default term and no emergency path
findings.quote: 2. The exception `MUST` be narrower and shorter-lived than the rule it varies.
findings.critique: The contract has ten record fields, eight MUSTs and one size. There is no default maximum term, so a five-year expiry is admissible; no short form for a team where requester and approver are the same accountable person; and no act-then-record path for an emergency. 'Shorter-lived than the rule' cannot be evaluated because rules have no lifetime. The strong parts risk being buried under form-filling.
findings.recommendation: Add: (a) an EXAMPLE default term, for instance 90 days for a MUST-level security rule with one renewal before the deviation goes to policy revision; (b) a minimum form: rule, scope, reason, owner, compensating control and expiry in the tracker suffice where one accountable person holds both roles; (c) an emergency path: act, then record within one working day; (d) reword rule 2 to 'narrower than the rule's scope and time-bound'.

findings.title: Audit pack offers an auditee-chosen sample and omits bypass records
findings.quote: Sample of last **N** merges with associated evidence bundle references
findings.critique: An assessor does not accept a sample the auditee picked. The pack needs the complete population for the period so that the assessor can sample, and it omits the records assessors ask for first: every bypass or override of a required check, changes to protection rules, emergency changes with their retrospective, and who is able to change the gates.
findings.recommendation: Replace with: an export of all merges and deployments in the period, with the query that produced it, from which the assessor samples; every bypass, override, protection-rule change and emergency change with its approval and review; and the list of identities able to change gates or approve exceptions, with the date that list was last reviewed.

findings.title: Privileged-automation steps serve agents, not pipelines
findings.quote: The executor checks declared tools, policies, and packs first; a missing required dependency fails closed.
findings.critique: The title promises rules for any automation that can change real systems, but the five implementation steps are written for model-driven agents in library vocabulary (run contract, verifier packs, autonomy position, capability tier) that the page neither explains nor links to the glossary. An engineer who owns a deploy pipeline or a scheduled job gets one paragraph under 'variations' and does not finish the page knowing what to configure.
findings.recommendation: Make the normal implementation the deterministic case: protect and review the definition; give each job its own least-privilege identity; require approval on the production environment; restrict who and what can trigger it; pin third-party steps; give untrusted triggers no secrets; keep the evidence record. Move the agent-specific steps to a variation and explain each term on first use or link its glossary entry.

findings.title: Dependency adoption gives no adoption criteria
findings.quote: | Propose | Describe why it is needed and how to verify it; flag it as a review hotspot. |

SHOULD: runtimes, frameworks and base images past end of support are tracked as open findings with an owner and a date.

findings.title: Dependency-automation tooling predates release-age delays
findings.quote: **Auto-merge** only for patch/minor per policy, with CI green; never blind-merge majors without review.
findings.critique: The page predates the registry worm incidents of the past eighteen months. It treats patch and minor updates as the safe class for auto-merge, although the attacker chooses the version number, and it does not mention the release-age delay that both bots it compares now provide. library_recommendations.title: Decide ADRs 0047 and 0046 before any further addition, then execute them
library_recommendations.problem: The two ADRs that subtract or restructure (move maintainer doctrine out of the consumer path, collapse the AI-native SDLC, retire private vocabulary) have sat Proposed and unread by the owner for 76 days, while eight additive ADRs were accepted in four days. A third of the library's capitalised MUSTs bind its maintainers, and the vocabulary ADR 0046 set out to shrink has grown.
library_recommendations.recommendation: Owner reads both ADRs and records accept, reject or withdraw now rather than at the next sweep. If accepted: create doctrine/maintainers/ for the lifecycle, source-authority and change-harness patterns, the two registers and the change checklist; split the versioning pattern; collapse the SDLC pattern to at most 1,600 words; execute the vocabulary replacements; publish the normative-to-rationale word ratio in each sweep record.
library_recommendations.effort: 2 hours of owner reading for the decision; 1 to 2 days to execute
library_recommendations.confidence: high that the decision is overdue and that the measurements are right; medium that ADR 0047's exact shape is the best one

library_recommendations.title: Put one independent human domain review on record
library_recommendations.problem: No ADR records independent human or domain review. Every provenance line says model review only, every method record since August says class=generated, and the library has one author. By the library's own source-authority scale it is at best an S6 source and cannot by itself support a consumer's MUST.
library_recommendations.recommendation: Commission one named reviewer per high-stakes area, starting with supply chain (ADR 0053 and dependencies-supply-chain.md sections 3 to 5), then cryptography (ADR 0054) and statutory reporting (ADR 0055). Record role, date, findings and disposition in the ADR's Review provenance line. Add a second named maintainer in GOVERNANCE.md when one exists.
library_recommendations.effort: 1 to 2 reviewer-days per area, plus half a day to disposition findings

library_recommendations.title: State provenance and the real operating model at the front door
library_recommendations.problem: The disclosure that the text is model-drafted and model-reviewed exists only in ADRs and research notes. README.md, ENGINEERING.md, GOVERNANCE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, the TL;DR, how-to-read and the adoption playbook say nothing. GOVERNANCE.md describes review by 'another person' and names no maintainer, which is not how the library is run. The ADR index's provenance paragraph is stale.
library_recommendations.recommendation: Add two or three sentences to README.md and GOVERNANCE.md: who maintains the library, that drafting and review are done by models under one operator's direction, that no independent review is yet recorded, and that a MUST should be read as a referenced candidate rule to verify against its cited source. Refresh the ADR index paragraph.

library_recommendations.title: Freeze normative additions and tag the landed delta
library_recommendations.problem: Nine ADRs, including a normative tightening and new typed MUSTs, have been on main for up to 64 days with no tag. The versioning pattern says normative changes are signalled by tags. ENGINEERING.md tells consumers to pin v0.5.0 while its route table links 13 pages that tag does not contain. The v0.6.0 gate includes human cold-reader verification, so the unreleased delta keeps growing.
library_recommendations.recommendation: Stop accepting obligation-changing ADRs until a tag ships. Either cut v0.6.0 with the November delta and carry the unmet gates forward explicitly, or decouple the human-walkthrough gate and schedule it. Track days-since-tag and unreleased-ADR count in the sweep record.
library_recommendations.effort: 0.5 to 1 day including the release-coupled sweep
library_recommendations.confidence: high on the measurements; medium on which release mechanics the owner should choose

library_recommendations.title: Finish typing the classical core by deciding old claims, not adding new ones
